title: Maximal coherence of quantum measurement and the resource theory of sharpness
authors: Kyunghyun Baek, Yonggi Jo, Hyunchul Nha
abstract: A resource theory of quantum measurement can be addressed in terms of quantum coherence and measurement sharpness, respectively. The former analyzes the off-diagonal structure of POVM elements in a predetermined basis while the latter analyzes the deviation from trivial, state-independent, measurements. We establish a direct connection between the two resource theories by identifying measurement sharpness as the maximal coherence that is achievable under all possible unitary changes of the reference basis. For a broad class of POVMs whose elements share a common eigenbasis, we show that the maximal distance-based coherence of measurement coincides exactly with the corresponding distance-based sharpness monotone. We further extend this equivalence, with element-additive distances, to POVMs whose elements admit a common mutually unbiased basis structure. These results provide a measurement-theoretic analogue of the maximal-coherence \& purity correspondence for quantum states. We also show that the maximal coherence of measurement is faithful with respect to trivial measurements and is monotonic under fuzzifying operations for dichotomic measurements, as well as under mixed-unitary and unitarily covariant preprocessing channels. Finally, we illustrate the operational meaning and limitations of the equivalence through qubit POVMs, single-photon phase sensing, and noisy photon-number resolving detection. In particular, the maximal Fisher information in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer is shown to be determined by the squared maximal coherence of the measurement, while in an imperfect photon-number resolving detector the maximal coherence behaves as a proper sharpness monotone, unlike conventional PVM-based unsharpness measures.
summary: This paper develops a resource theory linking quantum coherence and measurement sharpness for POVMs. It proves that these two quantities coincide when the measurement elements share specific structural properties (like a common eigenbasis). The work provides operational diagnostics, showing how maximal coherence can quantify phase sensitivity in interferometers and correctly characterize imperfect detectors.
main_problem: To establish a precise quantitative relationship between two resource quantities associated with quantum measurements: quantum coherence and measurement sharpness.
main_result: Maximal coherence of measurement ($C_{\max}^D$) is shown to coincide exactly with the corresponding distance-based sharpness monotone ($S_D$) under specific structural conditions, providing an analogue to state purity correspondences.
method: The authors define both quantities using resource theory frameworks based on minimizing distances (like the diamond distance) over sets of trivial or reference measurements.
model_or_system: The study analyzes general quantum measurements described by Positive Operator-Valued Measures (POVMs) $\{A_x\}_{x=1}^n$ acting on a $d$-dimensional Hilbert space. Physical examples include Mach-Zehnder interferometers and noisy photon-number resolving detectors.

important_parameters: The equivalence holds when POVM elements share a common eigenbasis or admit a common mutually unbiased basis (MUB) structure.
main_assumptions: The equivalence theorems rely on the structural assumption that the POVM elements share a common eigenbasis or MUB structure; otherwise, $C_{\max}^D$ and $S_D$ may diverge.

paper_structure: The paper develops resource theories for measurement, defining $C_{\max}^D$ via basis optimization and $S_D$ via fuzzifying operations. It then proves the equivalence theorems under specific structural assumptions and validates these results using physical examples like interferometry.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical framework connecting two fundamental concepts in quantum measurement theory—coherence and sharpness—using resource theories, which is highly relevant for understanding measurement limitations in quantum optics and sensing.

Figure 3. Comparison of sharpness measures for the imperfect PNRD as a function of quantum efficiency η. All measures are normalized to the unit interval, and unsharpness measures are converted to sharpness via 1 −US. The HS norm and the measures of Baek, Mitra, and Liu–Luo are non-monotonic in η, reaching a maximum at both η = 0 (vacuum-projecting trivial measurement) and η = 1 (ideal PNRD). Only Buscemi et al.’s measure and the maximal coherence of measurement are monotonic, vanishing on the trivial measurement and in- creasing to the maximum on the ideal PNRD, hence both qualify as valid sharpness monotones in the resource theory of sharpness.
